text:
maria: Heads-up: customer 'TextFlow' reporting a spike of 502/504s from our hosted API in eu-west-1, started ~08:22 UTC. They see failures mainly during long streaming completions. sample request-id: req_0a3b7f2c, trace: trace-9f8a.

raj: Thanks Maria — do we have traces for req_0a3b7f2c? any upstream 5xx or envoy resets in the logs?

maria: Pushed logs + small snippet: `edge-proxy: upstream reset (rst_stream), code=2` then `502` returned to client. Stack shows h2 GOAWAY on upstream node. I'll paste the short log: 
```
2026-03-16T08:22:31Z edge-proxy[envoy] trace:req_0a3b7f2c upstream:10.2.4.17:443 rst_stream
2026-03-16T08:22:31Z upstream[model-srv-17] warn: kv cache miss, cold start
2026-03-16T08:22:32Z edge-proxy: 502 -> client
```

sam: interesting — kv cache miss then rst_stream. could be upstream OOM or overload causing h2 flow/window reset. any pod restarts around that time?

maria: No pod restarts in k8s events. CPU/GPU metrics for that node show GPU saturations but not OOM. Throughput jumps correlate with heavy batch of long-sequence chat messages from that tenant.

anya: @raj @ops-oncall can we get the envoy stats (h2 streams, rst, goaway counters) for the midproxy cluster for that minute? also check keepalive timeouts between edge and upstream.

infra-bot: pulled envoy admin /stats at 2026-03-16T08:25:00Z and uploaded to /internal/supp/1755554321/envoy-stats.log (expires in 72h).

raj: Quick skim: goaway_sent and rst_streams spiked on node pool-3 around 08:22. h2 connection window available dropped to near zero. Looks like many concurrent long streams causing send-window exhaustion + upstream buffer backpressure.

maria: Customer says failures happen when they send a 90k token context with streaming. We throttle embeddings/batches for them but not long chat windows.

sam: repro plan: 1) simulate a few concurrent long streaming requests to model-srv-17 from a test client in eu-west-1 2) capture envoy admin stats 3) try with adjusted keepalive and h2 initial window.

anya: Workaround suggestion to customer: reduce client-side concurrency to 2 for long sequences, or use non-streaming (buffered) endpoint for now. Will that be acceptable?

maria: Customer ok with temporary concurrency cap, asks for root cause and permanent fix.

raj: Hypothesis: continuous batching + long KV cache cold starts cause bursts of upstream send buffer growth. Envoy by default enforces per-connection h2 window; when windows are exhausted, envoy issues rst_stream to free resources and returns 502. Two-pronged fix: a) tune envoy h2 window and keepalive with upstream pool b) add graceful backpressure at router to limit concurrent long streaming passes to a single model shard.

sam: Quick mitigation applied: reduced max_concurrent_streams for the midproxy-to-upstream route from 100 -> 30 (can rollback). Also added temporary route-level circuit breaker (max connections 50).

infra-bot: config patch deployed to canary (midproxy-pool-3) at 2026-03-16T09:10:02Z: patch id cfg-7551.

maria: After mitigation customer reports failures dropped to near-zero in the next 10 minutes.

ops-oncall: Need a follow-up: 1) run load repro with long sequence to validate 502s gone 2) evaluate kernel-level TCP send buffer sizing and upstream model server batching window 3) consider model-serving change to stream partial tokens earlier to avoid large buffer build-up.

raj: I'll run the repro this afternoon and capture pcap + envoy stats. Also adding a regression alert for h2_goaway/rst ratio > 0.01.

anya: Also flagging for product: content/limits guidance — long contexts + high concurrency are a known risk; we should document recommended concurrency limits per model/instance type.

maria: Customer emailed a small test script. dropping it here for triage: 
```bash
# reproducer (use test api key)
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-13b-quant","input": "'$(python -c 'print("x "*30000)')'", "stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood-hosted.eu-west-1/v1/stream/generate
```

sam: Perfect — I'll run it against canary and prod with low concurrency and capture differences.

maria: Thanks all. tagging customer with our mitigation steps and ETA for follow-up report. :white_check_mark:
